newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - TIMELINES - Today in History - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - TIMELINES - Today in History - Feb 17.

text.p: *** BIRTHDAYS ***
Australian poet and author of the popular "Waltzing Matilda", ANDREW 'BANJO' PATTERSON, was born on this day in 1864.
Australian entertainer and creator of "Dame Edna Everidge" and "Sir Les Patterson", BARRY HUMPHRIES, was born in 1934.
British actor ALAN BATES ("Far from the Madding Crowd") was born in 1934.

Popular American singer GENE PITNEY was born in 1941. He wrote the hit songs "He's A Rebel" for the 'Crystals' and "Hello Mary Lou" for RICKY NELSON. He recorded as a solo artist from 1960 to 1968. His biggest hits were "(The Man Who Shot) Liberty Valance" (1962), "Only Love Can Break A Heart" (1962), "It Hurts To Be In Love" (1964) and "I'm Gonna Be Strong". After a long absence he reappeared in the charts with MARC ALMOND with a remake of "Something's Gotten Hold Of My Heart" (1989).
US child singing star DODIE STEVENS (GERALDINE ANN PASQUALE) was born in 1947. When she was 11 she had a hit with "Pink Shoe Laces" (1959).
*** EVENTS ***
1883 : The VACANT/ENGAGED toilet-door sign was patented
by an Englishman known as Mr ASHWELL.
1909 : American Indian (Apache) Chief GERONIMO died at
the age of 80. In 1881 he led the last Apache uprising against US forces in Arizona and New Mexico, and passed away on a Reservation, far from the homeland he'd defended.
1916 : The British government appealed against the use of
motor cars and motor cycles for pleasure.
1917 : The German government finally signed the Armistice
giving up territory to Poland.
1926 : A British doctor warned that many modern young

women were turning to drink and drugs in a "desperate bid to cope with their hectic lives". Dr RUSSELL told the London Institute of Hygiene that increasingly popular lifestyle of some young women was ageing them prematurely. He said "nights of frivolity followed by days of excitement, coupled with tobacco and alcohol, strained the nervous system." His criticism followed warnings about the trend for women to attempt to acquire a "willowy figure". The doctors said the trend to look like "weak and weedy men" could increase the risk of consumption.
1935 : A daily air passenger service began between
Canberra and Sydney.
1958 : The "Ban The Bomb" CAMPAIGN FOR NUCLEAR
DISARMAMENT group was formed in Britain, spurred by the threat of American nuclear weapons on British soil.
1968 : French Alpine skier JEAN-CLAUDE KILLY won all 3
Men's Gold medals at the Winter Olympic Games in Grenoble, France.
1972 : The VW BEETLE reached worldwide sales of
15-million, overtaking the MODEL-T FORD.
1972 : In London the Commons passed a bill to bring
Britain into the European Economic Community.
1972 : American actor ROCK HUDSON arrived in Australia to
present the TV Logie Awards.
1979 : China invaded Vietnam, just a month after
Vietnamese forces had driven POL POT and his murderous KHMER ROUGE (which China had supported) out of Cambodia.
1982 : Jazz pianist and composer THELONIUS MONK,
influential in the "bop" sound, died.
1989 : British police confirmed that the Lockerie air

crash was caused by a bomb hidden in a radio cassette player. The Pan American jumbo jet crashed into the Scottish border town on December 21st 1988 killing all 259 passengers and 11 people on the ground.
